description: NIST's FTC-11, its AP242 edition 2's solid #1299 alone (the excerpt beside blend/nist-ftc-11-ap242-bspline-circle-fillet): the convex plane-against-plane edge e24 filleted alone at the battery's radius. It is the first of a tangent chain of three on the plane f0: the line e24, the edge e25 between f0 and the cylinder f19 written as a cubic B-spline that hides a circle (r 0.1063, within 4.4e-4 of the faces' own section, its tolerance 2.5e-3), and the line e26. At v24 the hole f17 runs on from f18 at a convex kink of 3.9°, tangent within the vertex's tolerance and not the faces', and the contact on the top misses the hole: the chain runs on through the kink (ADR-0075) to e22 and e23, five edges, as Open CASCADE's five blend faces, and Arris refuses it TangentChain naming e22 to e26, e60 and v24 until the junction across the kink is built. Open CASCADE builds it valid; the second oracle refuses it (plans/nurbs-face-blend step 1, plans/tolerant-tangency step 1). The desired result is the chain's blend, its junction across v24 the two runs' mean ball's arc (plans/tolerant-tangency step 5)
